parts.note: un is the French for 'a', the continental article
to shroud something is to cover it

explanation.surface: Someone lays bare a European burial cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: To expose something is to lay it bare or reveal it.

parts.note: read as a single unit's own power, but it is the name for a British council that runs all local services alone

explanation.surface: A question about the power belonging to a single person.
explanation.walkthrough: A unitary authority is a type of single-tier local council in the UK; the word itself means relating to one unit, hence 'One's individual'.
explanation.definitionFit: Describing a single whole unit, as in a one-tier council, which is the sense of being one's own individual.

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, above, the second

parts.note: competence means capability, the ability to do something
brown is a colour

explanation.surface: A gardener's skill is said to outweigh a hue.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancelot 'Capability' Brown was the great 18th-century English landscape gardener; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The most famous English landscape designer, who laid out the grounds of many country houses.

parts.note: to vie is to compete

explanation.surface: Someone rivals an outlook from the West.
explanation.definitionFit: A view is a personal opinion or way of seeing a matter.

parts.note: Rex is Latin for king, abbreviated R

indicators.note: something injured is damaged and bent out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bold man called Rex gets hurt on the slopes.
explanation.walkthrough: Rex is the Latin for king, so it stands for R as on coins and royal signatures; 'injured' looks like part of the story but is the anagram signal for 'skiing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Daring and risking both mean venturing or chancing something dangerous.

parts.note: the Aberdeen breed is a small Scottish hunting dog of a well-known group

explanation.surface: A question about a dog that comes from a Scottish city.
explanation.walkthrough: The Aberdeen is another name for the Scottish breed of small dog; the question mark marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish or Aberdeen breed is one of the small burrowing hunting dogs of that group.

parts.note: a horse going at a moderate pace is relatively fast, and a pig's foot is eaten as food

explanation.surface: A question about food that is quite quick to prepare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast food' suggests burgers; instead a horse bred for trotting moves relatively fast, and a pig's foot is a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A pig's foot cooked as a dish, and also a horse that moves at a brisk gait.

definitions.meaning: a small marsh bird of the crake family
the steel track a locomotive's wheels pass over

explanation.surface: A bird is killed by a passing train.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a wading marsh bird and the metal bar of a railway track that trains travel along.

parts.note: 'the nick' is slang for prison, so being locked up there for a time is just at the last moment

explanation.surface: A question about someone being jailed at the worst possible time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The nick' is British slang for prison, so 'in the nick' reads as imprisoned.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for arriving or acting just before it is too late.

parts.note: 'put on the map' usually means made famous, but here means literally drawn onto a map a second time

explanation.surface: Something becomes famous once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To map something afresh, drawing its plan a second time.

clue.text: Ironic pessimist possibly giving the general idea

indicators.note: possibly signals that these letters may be another arrangement of the same words

explanation.surface: A gloomy person with a wry outlook offers a rough outline.
explanation.definitionFit: Impressionistic means conveying an overall sense rather than detail.

indicators.note: unfinished means the word for church loses its last letter

parts.note: an abbey is a church of a monastery

explanation.surface: A Parisian cleric's place of worship has not been completed.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbé is the title of a French cleric or abbot.

indicators.note: into means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Pte is the abbreviation for the army rank of private
one is I, and 's is is, giving I plus S

explanation.surface: Someone forces their way onto a private, well-trodden path.
explanation.definitionFit: A piste is a ski run of compacted, beaten-down snow.

clue.text: Star, say, entering one of the eastern states

indicators.note: entering means one piece goes into the other

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for Virginia, a state on the US east coast
say means for example, abbreviated eg

explanation.surface: A celebrity, for instance, moves into an East Coast state.
explanation.definitionFit: Vega is the brightest star in the constellation Lyra.

parts.note: Piraeus is the port of Athens, so the letter is a character of the Greek script, the very first one

explanation.surface: Someone receives a piece of mail sent from a Greek port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' suggests correspondence; it is a character of the alphabet used in Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha is the first character of the Greek alphabet.

parts.note: up means excited or worked up
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A thrilled team suffers a loss.
explanation.definitionFit: An upset is an unexpected defeat of a favourite.

parts.note: a blazer is something burning, and the present time is the season of gifts

explanation.surface: A jacket that is fashionable today.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blazer' suggests a jacket and 'present time' now; it means a burning log at the time of presents, Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: A large log burnt on the hearth at Christmas, or a chocolate cake made to look like one.

parts.note: an impression here is a print run of a book, not an opinion

explanation.surface: A remark about forming a further opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: A fresh print run of a book, which a publisher calls a further impression.

clue.text: Abandoned, having fallen by the wayside?

definitions.meaning: literally having fallen into the trench at the side of a road

explanation.surface: Something left behind, as if it has dropped out along the way.
explanation.definitionFit: Both cast off, and literally landed in a roadside trench.

clue.text: Sound from tenth ringer cut short

parts.note: deci- is the prefix meaning a tenth

indicators.note: cut short means the word for the ringer loses its last letter

parts.note: a bell is something that rings

explanation.surface: A noise comes from the tenth bell, abruptly stopped.
explanation.definitionFit: A decibel is the unit measuring the loudness of a noise.

clue.text: Song in the act performed later

indicators.note: in means the word for song is placed within the word for act

parts.note: a deed is an act
a lay is a song or ballad

explanation.surface: A song included in a stage act is put on after the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Delayed means put off or carried out after the due time.

definitions.meaning: a routine physical examination by a doctor
to investigate or confirm something thoroughly

explanation.surface: A doctor's examination is meant to confirm everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a routine health examination and, as a phrasal verb, to inspect thoroughly.

parts.note: a harvester is one who gathers crops, and 'come a' one of those means fail badly

explanation.surface: A question about a farmer's failed harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come a cropper' is a British idiom for falling heavily or failing.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who harvests crops, and the word in the idiom for a heavy fall or failure.

indicators.note: capsizing means overturning, so the letters of the fan are tumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A rock fan tips over in a small boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirogue is a long narrow dugout boat.

clue.text: A young reporter first on the island

indicators.note: first means the young reporter comes before the letter A

parts.note: a cub is a novice or junior journalist

explanation.surface: A junior journalist is the first to land on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuba is the largest island in the Caribbean.

indicators.note: inside means the first letter is put within the barrier

parts.note: a boom is a floating barrier across a harbour or river

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of leafy

explanation.surface: A flower and its leaves first appear within a fence.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloom is a blossom on a plant.

clue.text: Can be seen in the safari from a long way off

indicators.note: can be seen in means the letters are visible inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: On safari, animals are viewed from a distance.
explanation.definitionFit: Afar means at or from a great distance.

parts.note: I had shortens to I'd

explanation.surface: Someone recalls having a scheme for everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea is a plan or notion in the mind.

clue.text: Telephone leading lady in western state

indicators.note: in means the first letter goes within the abbreviation for the state

parts.note: Cal is an abbreviation for California, a state in the American West

indicators.note: leading means the first letter of lady

explanation.surface: Someone phones the female star living in California.
explanation.definitionFit: To call someone is to ring or phone them.

clue.text: In a local accent more or less

definitions.meaning: talking with a strong regional pronunciation

explanation.surface: Talking with a regional accent, approximately.
explanation.definitionFit: Both talking with a heavy regional brogue and an idiom meaning in general terms.

indicators.note: round means the fat goes around the other piece

parts.note: lard is fat smeared in cooking
any can mean some, as in 'have you any?'

explanation.surface: A little grease has been rubbed around a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A lanyard is a short cord or line, used on ships or worn round the neck.

clue.text: Help one in need mitigate pain

explanation.surface: Assist someone struggling by easing their suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: Both to come to someone's aid and to ease or alleviate discomfort.
